I know this is an old article, but I feel like this part could be cleaned up a bit:

It could be a Type I, a telekinetic vector associated with a deceased person, but field agents said that there's considerable domestic strife in the home. It's most likely undifferentiated kinetic energy from a latent Bixby under extreme stress. Type II.

I would assume that the elite MTF soldiers know what Type I and II mean, so it feels kind of exposition-y. Writing them up in footnotes would work better IMO.

item.content:encoded:
I like the world you've made. In terms of creating a spooky universe, where the real kick comes from what you don't know, it functions a lot like 173, but a more fleshed out version. I like it. This is an example of something from the first series that fits the atmosphere and style of then, but fulfills our current standards as well. Not only that, it does an exploration log realistically, although the dialogue was a bit stiff (mostly this particular line: "no, those darts aren't calibrated!". This sentence just feels clunky.) It also acts as a simple 'glitch' in the universe much like other early entries, and around this a story is built.

All in all, it's like a standard SCP article. If you gave someone who asked "What is the SCP foundation?" this could definitely be one to use. It even fits in a punchline.

item.content:encoded:
The issues I have with this are not outweighing the technical skill involved in drafting the article, so I'll register a neutral vote here.

The scientific treatment is convincing enough that I can buy that it's accurate, or at least enough to fool a layperson such as myself into believing it's accurate, which is really the standard we ought to be shooting for. The connection to the hamster is a bit silly, but mostly I feel between all the strikeout text and the recovery log, this article drags a bit as I read it. I feel it could do with some streamlining; I don't mind exceptionally dry tone in places at all (in fact, I encourage it in some places), but when you're relying on it as heavily as you are in this piece, it's not a bad idea to adjust the rest of the article to account for the overall experience for the reader.

TL;DR Not bad, but it drags a little bit too much for my tastes. Neutral.

item.content:encoded:
Ooh, I should have kept in the archived containment procedures!

(Because, essentially, that's what they were before the rewrite.)

For the curious, here they are (the original procedures):

ARCHIVED CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES - FOR LOG PURPOSES ONLY
FOLLOW ABOVE PROCEDURES - DO NOT ATTEMPT BELOW

SCP-128 is to be kept in a chamber measuring at least 10 m x 10 m x 5 m with walls and door armored in 5 cm steel plate. All personnel who enter the containment room must wear full suits of heavy body armor, including ballistic plates. All loose objects of mass greater than 5 kg are strictly prohibited. Clothing and related items are generally considered safe, as the entity appears to be incapable of distinguishing these from their wearers. Writing utensils, loose change, and other trinkets present considerable hazards to personnel and should therefore be used sparingly never enter the containment chamber.

All items are to be cleared from room via suction before any personnel will be permitted to enter. Once personnel have exited, SCP-128 is to be given small objects, both to study its behavior and to alleviate boredom (if applicable). In the event of escape, the surrounding area will be evacuated and locked down, possibly followed by attempts to herd SCP-128 back into its enclosure. Past experience suggests that the latter is unnecessary, as the entity has shown no apparent desire to vacate the premises and will eventually return of its own accord.
